verified_claims: Lemma 1: the sequence is well-defined (product of previous terms witnesses a candidate), strictly increasing, unbounded, and equals the increasing enumeration of S_inf ∩ [a_1,∞); the converse direction (any x in S_inf with x≥a_1 must be a term, else minimality of a_{n+1} gives a_{n+1}≤x) is correct.
Lemma 2 (killing property): for x>a_1 not in S_inf, minimality of a_{n+1} forces gcd(x,a_i)=1 for some earlier term a_i<x; verified including the edge case a_1<x<a_2.

Lemma 3: S_inf is closed under multiples; every element has a divisibility-minimal divisor in S_inf (finite divisor set argument); minimal elements are squarefree; C is exactly the family of minimal transversals of the support family and M={π(t):t∈C}; C is an antichain; all members of C are nonempty finite sets; M,C ≠ ∅ (apply (a) to a_1).
Lemma 4: permanents pairwise intersect — π(t)^k ≥ a_1 is a term with support t, and any t'∈C meets that support.

Lemma 5 (self-duality for finite minimal transversals): verified step by step (T meets supp(a_i) for all i since T meets the permanent t ⊆ supp(a_i); π(T)∈S_inf; some t'⊆T in C; t' is a transversal by Lemma 4; minimality gives T=t'∈C).
Lemma 6: killing in permanent form — Lemma 2 plus Lemma 3(a) yields a permanent disjoint from F with strictly smaller π-value.

Lemma 7: cofactor reduction — the minimality of π(t*) among permanents containing q, combined with π(F)∉S_inf (proper divisor of a minimal element) and Lemma 6, forces π(t*\{q}) ≤ a_1; the chain π(t)<π(F)=π(t*)/q<π(t*) is valid; the degenerate case F=∅ is impossible under the contradiction hypothesis since π(∅)=1≤a_1.

Theorem (finiteness of C): union of an infinite antichain of finite sets contains infinitely many primes; only finitely many primes ≤ a_1, so infinitely many q_j>a_1; Lemma 7 plus pigeonhole over subsets of primes ≤ a_1 gives infinitely many t_j = s∪{q_j} with fixed s and q_j∉s; every u∈C meets s (else finite u would contain infinitely many distinct q_j, using Lemma 4); a transversal u_0⊆s minimal among transversals contained in s is globally minimal (any smaller transversal is a subset of u_0⊆s); Lemma 5 gives u_0∈C, and u_0⊆s⊊s∪{q_j} contradicts the antichain property (q_j∉s guarantees proper containment).

Lemma 8: with M finite and L=lcm(M), membership in S_inf is equivalent to divisibility by some h_i, hence m∈S_inf ⇔ m+L∈S_inf; x↦x+L is an order-preserving bijection between the indicated half-lines; each block [a_1+jL, a_1+(j+1)L) contains exactly T=|S_inf∩[a_1,a_1+L)|≥1 elements {x+jL}; therefore a_{jT+r}=a_r+jL and a_{n+T}=a_n+L for all n≥1 (decomposition n=jT+r with T≥1 is valid).

No circularity in the dependency order: 1→{2,3,4}→{5,6}→7→Theorem→(with Lemma 8) conclusion; edge cases (empty F, empty s, q_j∈s, singleton permanents, C infinite implying nonempty) are all handled or cannot occur.

Sanity checks on small instances (a_1=2,4,6 give even numbers with T=1, L=2; a_1=15 gives a nontrivial start 15,18,20,24,30,36,40,42,45,...) are consistent with the enumeration and periodicity claims.
summary: The proof is correct, complete, and self-contained. The chain of reductions — greedy sequence = increasing enumeration of the stable set S_inf (Lemma 1); killing property from greedy minimality (Lemmas 2, 6); reduction of large primes in permanents to bounded cofactors (Lemma 7); self-duality of the minimal-transversal family (Lemma 5) combined with the antichain property to force finiteness of the permanents (Theorem); and periodicity from invariance of S_inf under shifts by the lcm of the finitely many minimal elements (Lemma 8) — closes all gaps, including degenerate cases (empty cofactor, empty s, comparability contradiction). Two presentational compressions (the one-line reason a transversal minimal within s is globally minimal, since any smaller transversal lies in u_0⊆s; and the explicit existence/uniqueness of n with a_n<x<a_{n+1}) are easily supplied and do not affect correctness. Each lemma was independently re-derived and checked against counterexample scenarios (e.g., the antichain {p_1,q} family is correctly ruled out via self-duality plus descent, not by antichain/pairwise-intersection properties alone).
transfer_assessment: Reusable: identifying a greedy/minimal-choice sequence with the increasing enumeration of its 'stable' target set S_inf (Lemma 1) — a general device converting recursive minimality into a membership characterization with a killing property (Lemma 2).

Reusable: passing from divisibility-minimal elements of a gcd-defined set to squarefree representatives and minimal transversals of a support hypergraph (Lemma 3), converting a number-theoretic dynamics question into hypergraph combinatorics.

Reusable: self-duality of the minimal-transversal family (Lemma 5) — every finite minimal transversal of C lies in C — a standard but powerful hypergraph duality argument driven here by pairwise intersection (Lemma 4) and by every term being a multiple of a minimal element.

Reusable: descent/cofactor-bounding argument (Lemmas 6–7): apply the killing property to π(t*\{q}) to produce a cheaper permanent containing q, bounding the cofactor by a_1; then pigeonhole over the finitely many small cofactors and derive an antichain contradiction — the essential mechanism forcing finiteness.

Reusable: periodicity transfer (Lemma 8): if a set is a finite union of multiple-sets with lcm L, it is invariant under x↦x+L, so its increasing enumeration satisfies a_{n+T}=a_n+L with T the block count — converts multiplicative periodicity into additive arithmetic periodicity.

Misleading if transferred without care: antichain + pairwise-intersecting alone do NOT imply finiteness (e.g., all pairs containing a fixed prime), so any ported argument must retain the greedy descent (Lemmas 2/6/7); also Lemma 5's self-duality is claimed only for finite transversals and relies on the specific structure, so it cannot be quoted as a general hypergraph fact.
